title: Battery module coolant loop
description:
Design the liquid cooling loop for a battery module of 12 cells on one cold plate. Each cell carries I = 120 A through R_cell = 0.49 mOhm, so q_cell = I^2 * R_cell and the plate absorbs Q_heat = N_cells * q_cell. Choose a coolant, a pump, the pump speed fraction s (0.3 to 1.0), the cold-plate channel inner diameter d, and the number of parallel channels n_par (1 to 4).

Cold plate: n_par identical channels of diameter d and length L_ch = 0.528 m in parallel; the flow and the heat split equally between them. Loop piping: one run of inner diameter 12 mm, length 5.21 m, total fittings loss coefficient K = 12.3, carrying the whole flow. Coolant enters the plate at T_in = 15 C (chiller).

Hydraulics: v = (Qv / n_par) / (pi d^2 / 4), Re = rho v d / mu. Friction factor f = 64 / Re for Re < 2300, else Blasius f = 0.316 Re^-0.25. dP_channel = f (L_ch / d) rho v^2 / 2. dP_pipe = (f_pipe L_pipe / d_pipe + K) rho v_pipe^2 / 2 with the pipe's own Re and f. dP_system = dP_channel + dP_pipe. Pump at speed fraction s follows the affinity laws: dP_pump(Qv) = s^2 * curve(Qv / s), electrical power P_pump = P_rated * s^3, where curve() is the full-speed pressure vs flow table interpolated linearly. The operating point is where dP_pump = dP_system.

Thermal: T_out = T_in + Q_heat / (rho Qv cp). Pr = mu cp / k. Nu = 4.36 for Re < 2300, else Dittus-Boelter Nu = 0.023 Re^0.8 Pr^0.4. h = Nu k / d. Heat flux per channel q'' = (Q_heat / n_par) / (pi d L_ch). Hottest cell (at the outlet): T_cell = T_out + q'' / h + q_cell * R_cp with cell-to-plate resistance R_cp = 0.22 K/W.

Properties: evaluate rho, cp, mu, k at T_mean = (T_in + T_out) / 2 by linear interpolation in the table below, clamped outside it. T_out depends on the properties, so solve self-consistently.

Constraints: coolant freeze point <= site minimum temperature -5 C; channel Re must be <= 2000 or >= 3000 (no transitional flow); T_cell <= 25 C; T_out - T_in <= 4 C; channel velocity v <= 1.5 m/s; P_pump <= 15 W; cost = pump price + n_par * L_ch * tube price per metre <= 26.

Coolants:
  WATER: freeze point 0 C; at T = 10, 30, 50 C: rho = 1002 / 997.3 / 990 kg/m3, cp = 4179 / 4172 / 4171 J/(kg K), mu = 1.304 / 0.801 / 0.548 mPa s, k = 0.5817 / 0.6161 / 0.643 W/(m K)
  MEG-30: freeze point -14.6 C; at T = 10, 30, 50 C: rho = 1041.8 / 1033.7 / 1023.4 kg/m3, cp = 3689 / 3747 / 3803 J/(kg K), mu = 2.983 / 1.639 / 1.041 mPa s, k = 0.4555 / 0.4741 / 0.4917 W/(m K)
  MEG-50: freeze point -36 C; at T = 10, 30, 50 C: rho = 1070 / 1059.4 / 1047.1 kg/m3, cp = 3258 / 3364 / 3459 J/(kg K), mu = 5.257 / 2.729 / 1.678 mPa s, k = 0.383 / 0.3953 / 0.4077 W/(m K)

Pumps:
  PMP-1: pressure vs flow at full speed [[0, 10728], [1.79, 8582], [2.86, 4828], [3.58, 0]] (L/min, Pa), rated electrical power 8.4 W, price 18.90
  PMP-2: pressure vs flow at full speed [[0, 17820], [3.56, 14256], [5.7, 8019], [7.13, 0]] (L/min, Pa), rated electrical power 16.1 W, price 25.48
  PMP-3: pressure vs flow at full speed [[0, 34090], [6.82, 27272], [10.91, 15340], [13.64, 0]] (L/min, Pa), rated electrical power 38.5 W, price 35.20
  PMP-4: pressure vs flow at full speed [[0, 47080], [9.42, 37664], [15.07, 21186], [18.83, 0]] (L/min, Pa), rated electrical power 76.2 W, price 60.14
  PMP-5: pressure vs flow at full speed [[0, 72800], [14.56, 58240], [23.3, 32760], [29.12, 0]] (L/min, Pa), rated electrical power 125.6 W, price 91.20

Channel tube (inner diameter, price per metre): 4 mm at 1.14/m, 6 mm at 1.18/m, 8 mm at 1.66/m, 10 mm at 2.47/m, 12 mm at 3.23/m.

Objective: minimize pump electrical power P_pump. A design passes only if it meets every constraint AND its P_pump is within 5% of the lowest P_pump among designs that meet every constraint. Return {"coolant": "<id>", "pump": "<id>", "speed": <0.3-1.0>, "channel_d_mm": <4|6|8|10|12>, "n_parallel": <1-4>}.
sources: NREL/CP-540-40446 Kim & Pesaran 2006, Battery Thermal Management System Design Modeling (US Gov): channel-cooling archetype, property-table pattern
DOE/AMO Improving Pumping System Performance sourcebook (US Gov): pump affinity laws
CoolProp incompressible library (MIT): INCOMP::Water, INCOMP::MEG-30%, INCOMP::MEG-50% property tables and freeze points
Dittus & Boelter 1930 (Univ. California Publ. Eng.) and Blasius 1913: turbulent tube correlations; laminar Nu = 4.36 (constant heat flux)
